cohort: The study included 100 prematurely born adults born very preterm (<32 weeks) and/or at very low birth weight (<1500 g), and 106 controls born at full term, with a mean age of 26.8 years.
finding: Enlargement of the lateral ventricle volume (LVV) and increased deep and periventricular white matter lesions (WMLs) are typical sequelae of premature birth identifiable on routine brain MRI in young adults.
birth_weight: <1500 g (for VLBW group), N/A for controls
gest_age: <32 weeks (for VP group), Full term (for controls)
